title: Policy 2021-02 remote processing and telepharmacy
rule_summary: Section V of Board Policy 2021-02 (adopted 2/19/21; revised 4/7/22 and 2/6/25) defines remote processing services as a system that allows the processing of patient-specific prescriptions outside the licensed pharmacy premises of a Massachusetts-licensed pharmacy without final product verification or dispensing responsibilities, and states that prescriptions may be processed outside those premises provided the processes are verified by a Massachusetts-licensed pharmacist or performed in a pharmacy licensed by the Board. A note adds that, in accordance with the Board's Scope of Practice policy, pharmacy technicians holding a Massachusetts pharmacy technician license may perform remote processing on behalf of a retail or institutional pharmacy located in Massachusetts without on-site supervision by a Massachusetts-licensed pharmacist. Section VI defines telepharmacy as the utilization of telecommunications technology to oversee aspects of pharmacy operations or provide patient care services, and limits the telepharmacy the policy allows to remote pharmacist verification of final patient-specific products and clinical activities by a pharmacist such as patient counseling, drug utilization review, and drug therapy monitoring. Telepharmacy activities must be conducted by a Massachusetts-licensed pharmacist or performed in a Board-licensed pharmacy; the Board-licensed pharmacy dispensing the final patient-specific product must have at least one licensed pharmacist on the premises; and technologies used for remote verification must be in good working order with, at a minimum, high definition image resolution with variable viewing options and sufficient data retention capabilities to investigate quality-related events.
exam_relevance: Tests the line between remote processing, which excludes final verification and dispensing, and telepharmacy remote verification, which still requires a pharmacist on the premises of the dispensing pharmacy.

authority.name: Board of Registration in Pharmacy Policy 2021-02: Shared Pharmacy Service Models Including Central Fill, Remote Processing, and Telepharmacy (adopted 2/19/21; revised 4/7/22 and 2/6/25)

numeric_facts.fact: minimum licensed pharmacists on the premises of the dispensing pharmacy using telepharmacy
numeric_facts.conditions: Board-licensed pharmacy dispensing the final patient-specific product; Policy 2021-02 VI(b)(ii)

common_confusions: Remote processing as the policy defines it carries no final product verification or dispensing responsibility.
Remote verification of the final product by telepharmacy does not remove the need for a licensed pharmacist on the dispensing pharmacy's premises.
